oracles: a local echo-server over USB (adb reverse) — TLS and HTTP/2, 5 samples
the local raw-header stand — HTTP/1.1, fetch, XHR, WebSocket
captured.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 10; K) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/152.0.0.0 Mobile Safari/537.36
captured.note: the JA4 matched chrome-152-windows: the TLS stack is the same one and the platform does not change the ClientHello. The profile differs only in its headers

tls.note: the GREASE in signature_algorithms changes between browser runs: the capture recorded 0xAAAA and the phone later sent 0xEAEA. The profile holds the marker 2570 and the value is drawn per connection. uTLS does not know the trust_anchors extension (0xCA34), so allow_blunt_mimicry is on

trust_anchors.note: the set matched between desktop Chrome 152 and Chrome on a Pixel 7. The browser shuffles the order: three runs gave three permutations of one set. The same extension arrives in the QUIC handshake too

headers.note: the HTTP/1.1, fetch, XHR and WebSocket templates matched desktop Chrome name for name, so they are inherited from chrome-152-windows. sec-fetch-site and sec-fetch-user in the profile are set for a typed-address navigation: the browser was launched by a command from another application and therefore sent cross-site without sec-fetch-user

not_measured: HTTP/3 and QUIC: Chromium demands a chain to a publicly known root for QUIC, and the stand is signed by its own CA — see docs/CAPTURE.md

client_hints.requested_via: Accept-CH in the stand's response; Critical-CH makes the request repeat at once
